source_refs.note: Organ pipe: a main subheading of 7.6 Stationary waves in air columns, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 150-150.

blocks.text: An organ pipe is a wind instrument in which sound is produced, due to setting up of stationary waves in air column. It consists of a hollow long tube with both ends open or with one end open and the other closed. The relationship between the incident wave and the reflected wave depends upon whether the reflecting end of the pipe is open or closed.

items: If the reflecting end is open, the air molecules have complete freedom of motion and this behaves as an antinode.
If the reflecting end is closed, then it behaves as a node because the movement of the molecules is restricted.
